subject: Cannot use annotation_custom twice in one plot for map

messages.author: 6a3b777d6a18967b
messages.subject: Cannot use annotation_custom twice in one plot for map
parts:
I am attempting to use ggplot2 to create a map of the 50 US states with Alaska and Hawaii as insets. After talking with members of the GIS community they recommended this method (insets) as opposed to modifying the shapefile to "move" AK and HI to the desired locations.  It appears that ggplot2 supports insets via the annotation_custom function.  However, I am finding that ggplot2 will only render one of my insets, and it's always the one I write first.

I am attaching the shapefiles and R code as attachments. I am also attaching screenshots.  Note that in my screenshots the grobs for AK and HI only show the axes, and AK is placed incorrectly - this is just because I am reproing the bug and removed some excess code that that prettified the image.

For reference, I created a github repo for my shapefile which explains where I got it from as well as the modifications I made for it.

Here is my code which reproduces the bug.  Am I using annotation_custom correctly?  Is there a bug in ggplot2 related to this particular situation?  Is there another way for me to accomplish what I am trying to do?

Thanks.

Ari

require("rgdal") # requires sp, will use proj.4 if installed
require("maptools")
require("ggplot2")
require("plyr")
require(gpcilb)
gpclibPermit()

# the smallest of the state shapefiles
setwd("~/R/choroplethr-maps/state")

# get the shapefile as a data.frame
us.states = readOGR(dsn=".", layer="gz_2010_us_040_00_20m")
us.states@data$id = rownames(us.states@data)
us.states.points = fortify(us.states, region="id")
us.states.df = join(us.states.points, us.states@data, by="id")

# separate contiguous states from Alaska and Hawaii
us.states.48 = us.states.df[!us.states.df$NAME %in% c("Alaska", "Hawaii"), ]
alaska.df = us.states.df[us.states.df$NAME=='Alaska',]
hawaii.df = us.states.df[us.states.df$NAME=='Hawaii',]

# render the lower 48
base = ggplot(us.states.48, aes(long, lat, group=group)) + geom_polygon() 

# render Alaska as a grob, so we can add it as an inset with annotation_custom
alaska.ggplot = ggplot(alaska.df, aes(long, lat, group=group)) + geom_polygon() 
alaska.grob = ggplotGrob(alaska.ggplot)

# render Hawaii as a grob, so we can add it as an inset with annotation_custom
hawaii.ggplot = ggplot(hawaii.df, aes(long, lat, group=group)) + geom_polygon()
hawaii.grob = ggplotGrob(hawaii.ggplot)

# If you attempt to render the base + both insets, only the first annotation renders

# Only Alaska shows up
base +
  annotation_custom(grob=alaska.grob, xmin=-100, xmax=-80, ymin=35, ymax=40) +
  annotation_custom(grob=hawaii.grob, xmin=-115, xmax=-105, ymin=25, ymax=30) 

# swap the order - Only Hawaii shows up
base +
  annotation_custom(grob=hawaii.grob, xmin=-115, xmax=-105, ymin=25, ymax=30) +
  annotation_custom(grob=alaska.grob, xmin=-100, xmax=-80, ymin=35, ymax=40)

messages.author: 066b54eefceeb668
messages.subject: Re: Cannot use annotation_custom twice in one plot for map
parts:
Try passing alaska.grob and hawaii.grob to grobTree()function (from grid package).


library(grid)
base +
 annotation_custom(grobTree(alaska.grob), xmin=-100, xmax=-80, ymin=35, ymax=40) +
 annotation_custom(grobTree(hawaii.grob), xmin=-115, xmax=-105, ymin=25, ymax=30)

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Cannot use annotation_custom twice in one plot for map
parts:
Since I spent a bit of time on this, another option is to use grid
viewports, but I was hoping that one of the real experts would step in
to provide the elegant solution...so thanks, Sandy!


library(grid)
library(ggplot2)
base = ggplot(us.states.48, aes(long, lat, group=group)) + geom_polygon()

theme_bw() + geom_polygon() + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-170, -150, -130))

theme_bw() + geom_polygon() + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-160, -155))

grid.newpage()

vp <- viewport(width = 1, height = 1)

basevp <- viewport(width = 0.9, height = 0.9, x = 0.55, y = 0.55)
print(base, vp = vp)
ak <- viewport(width = 0.25, height = 0.25, x = 0.23, y = 0.21)
print(alaska.ggplot, vp = ak)
hi <- viewport(width = 0.2, height = 0.2, x = 0.865, y = 0.21)
print(hawaii.ggplot, vp = hi)

This works, but the grobTree() idiom is much cleaner and you don't
have to play around with relative coordinates, so go with Sandy's
solution.

It does lead to the following question, though: why is grobTree()
necessary in this case? I played around with annotation_map() and
could augment the main 48 grob with Alaska and then Hawaii, but the
same game with annotation_custom() didn't fly, as the OP reported.

Thought you guys might appreciate seeing the final image.  I spent some time fiddling with custom scale limits to get something that fits with what I'm used to seeing with images like this.  

I'm attaching the code in case anyone is interested in it.

In the next version of the choroplethr package I plan to release this map as well as a similar county-level map.  Hopefully the next time that someone wants to make a state or county level choropleth map in R that includes all 50 states they'll be able to use my package to "just do it" without needing to make the same investment of time that I made.
